interactions.advice: Combining these can cause a severe, life-threatening drop in blood pressure. Do not use sildenafil within 24-48 hours of any nitrate. Seek emergency care if you faint, have chest pain or severe dizziness.
Together these significantly raise the risk of serious stomach or intestinal bleeding. Ask your doctor before combining; a safer pain reliever is usually recommended.
Combining aspirin with warfarin increases the risk of major bleeding. Only use this combination when a doctor has explicitly prescribed it, and get regular blood tests.
This combination strongly increases bleeding risk, especially in the stomach. Use paracetamol instead if possible and confirm with your doctor.
This combination is sometimes prescribed after a stent or heart attack, but it raises bleeding risk significantly. Never add aspirin to clopidogrel on your own.
Ibuprofen can reduce clopidogrel's effect on platelets while adding stomach bleeding risk. Ask your doctor before combining them.
Clarithromycin raises digoxin levels in the blood and can cause digoxin toxicity (nausea, visual changes, irregular heartbeat). Monitor closely with your doctor.
Amiodarone roughly doubles digoxin levels, risking toxicity. Your doctor usually reduces the digoxin dose and checks levels.
Ciprofloxacin can increase the blood-thinning effect of warfarin and risks serious bleeding. More frequent INR checks are needed.
Metronidazole increases warfarin's effect and can raise bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely during this combination.
Clarithromycin blocks the breakdown of simvastatin, greatly raising the risk of muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis). This combination should be avoided.
Clarithromycin can raise atorvastatin levels and increase muscle injury risk. Your doctor may pause the statin during the short antibiotic course.
Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure and muscle side-effect risk. The simvastatin dose should usually be limited to 20 mg while taking amlodipine.
This combination can push blood potassium dangerously high, which may cause irregular heart rhythm. Blood potassium must be checked regularly.
Taking potassium supplements with an ACE inhibitor can cause dangerous hyperkalemia. Do not take potassium unless a doctor prescribes it.
Ibuprofen weakens lisinopril's blood-pressure-lowering effect and can harm the kidneys, especially in the elderly or with dehydration.
Taking ibuprofen close to a low-dose aspirin dose can block aspirin's protective effect on the heart. Separate them by several hours and ask your doctor.
Combining two NSAIDs increases stomach irritation and bleeding risk without adding much benefit. Use only one when possible.
NSAIDs reduce the elimination of methotrexate, risking severe bone-marrow and kidney toxicity. Avoid this combination.
SSRIs (like sertraline) together with NSAIDs increase the risk of stomach bleeding. Paracetamol is usually a safer choice.
SSRIs (like fluoxetine) together with NSAIDs increase the risk of stomach bleeding. Paracetamol is usually a safer choice.
Sertraline can increase warfarin's effect and bleeding risk. Watch for unusual bleeding and monitor INR closely.
Fluoxetine can increase warfarin's effect and bleeding risk. Watch for unusual bleeding and monitor INR closely.
Regular, high-dose paracetamol can increase warfarin's effect. Use the lowest dose needed and keep use occasional unless your doctor agrees.
If furosemide lowers potassium, digoxin toxicity becomes more likely. Keep potassium in the normal range and check levels with your doctor.
NSAIDs can raise lithium levels in the blood and risk lithium toxicity. Lithium levels must be checked if an NSAID is used.
Amoxicillin can slow removal of methotrexate and increase side effects. Use this combination only under medical supervision.
